saints.name: St. Severinus of Noricum
saints.title: Abbot, Apostle of Noricum
saints.shortBlurb: A monk who came out of the East to shepherd a frightened Roman frontier as the Western Empire collapsed…
biography: Severinus would never speak of his birth or his past, though he had known the monastic life of the East; he appeared along the Danube in Noricum soon after the death of Attila in 453, when Roman rule was crumbling and the frontier peoples stood exposed to the barbarian migrations. He founded monasteries at Favianis and near Passau.

To the terrified population he was pastor and protector: he ransomed captives, fed the starving, gathered refugees into safer towns, and even organized their defense. The Alamannic chief Gibuld, struck by his boldness, freed seventy prisoners at his word, and Odoacer honored him; Severinus foretold that Odoacer would become king in Italy, and warned him his rule would last but fourteen years.

He died in his cell at Favianis on 8 January 482, singing the last psalm. Six years later his monks, driven out, carried his body to Italy, where it rests near Naples. His disciple Eugippius, who followed the relics, wrote his Life about 511, the chief record of the Danube frontier as the Western Empire fell; Austria and Bavaria honor him as patron.
saints.knownFor: Protecting the people of Noricum as Roman rule collapsed.
